mechanisms.name: `rotationPolicy` default: Never -> Always (HIGH, delayed)
resourcesConsumers: Certificate mesh-root-ca (root of the mTLS trust chain; ECDSA, prod duration 8760h, renewBefore 720h)
checkout service (verifies ledger with --cacert /tls/ca.crt; curl loop re-reads files on every call)
ledger Deployment (no reloader or checksum annotation)
mechanisms.mechanism: None of the Certificates set rotationPolicy, so the default flips from Never to Always for all three; the default is applied server-side at reissue time, so it is invisible in every diff (the "unchanged manifest" trap). Nothing breaks on upgrade day. At mesh-root-ca's first renewal after the upgrade a new root key is generated (under 1.17.2 it was reused), giving a different root. Old leaves do not verify against the new root and new leaves do not verify against the old root. Each service's ca.crt copy is written only when its own leaf is issued, so whichever leaf renews first gets a new-root cert and ca.crt while its peer keeps the old chain, and mutual verification fails in both directions until both sides have renewed. A second, compounding gap: ledger's nginx reads ssl_client_certificate at start or reload and does not re-read it when the mounted Secret changes, so after a root rotation ledger would keep trusting the old root until its pods restart. That nginx behaviour existed before but was harmless while the root key never changed. The default flip is what turns it into an outage. Leaves renew about 20 days after issuance (duration 720h, renewBefore 240h); the root renews 30 days before its 1-year expiry; the next root renewal date is unknown from the repo and 'could be days away'. Leaf keys will also rotate on renewal. The assessment calls this intended upstream and fine for a cert and key delivered together in one Secret, with a caveat: ledger's nginx will not load a renewed cert/key until restarted. That is unchanged by 1.18, but with 10 days between renewal and expiry it is a latent risk.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Easy to neutralise before the upgrade. In order of preference (both accepted by 1.17.2, so they can ship before the upgrade as a separate commit): 1) set spec.privateKey.rotationPolicy: Never explicitly on mesh-root-ca in platform/pki, and keep it until a deliberate root rotation procedure exists; 2) optionally also set it on the leaf Certificates for zero behaviour change (leaving them at Always is arguably better security); 3) values-level fallback config.featureGates.DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways: false, temporary only because upstream says the gate is removed in 1.19; 4) independently, fix the ledger reload gap (a reloader, or a checksum or rollout trigger) so that any future CA rotation is survivable.
citedEvidence: upstream/.../upgrading-1.17-1.18.md

mechanisms.mechanism: Direct ACME Challenge creation can bypass DNS01 solver policy. Affected versions are >= 1.18.0 and <= 1.20.2, with fixes only in 1.19.6 and 1.20.3. There is no 1.18.x fix, so 1.18.0 enters an affected range that 1.17.2 is outside, which makes 1.18.x a dead end for this advisory.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The repo declares only a CA issuer and a self-signed issuer, with no ACME or DNS01 solver. The assessment calls this a repo-level conclusion and says to check the live cluster for ClusterIssuers not declared here. For a long-term target, plan for 1.19.6+ and do not stop at 1.18.

overall.recommendation: Do not proceed as-is. Before upgrading, commit an explicit rotationPolicy: Never on mesh-root-ca (and decide on the leaves), sync it and confirm no reissue. Add a reload mechanism for ledger. Rehearse the upgrade and a forced root rotation in staging. Then upgrade in a quiet window, sequenced so cert-manager is healthy before pki and payments sync. Plan a documented root rotation procedure before ever setting Always on the root. The assessment also says to reconsider the version target: the latest 1.18.x patch at minimum, or 1.19.6+.
overall.quote: Do not proceed as-is. One documented breaking change creates a delayed outage risk for this environment. It is easy to neutralise before the upgrade.
